lessons.title: A telephone conversation: booking a bus seat
lessons.objective: Carry out a telephone conversation and carry out tasks on a text listened to.
lessons.course:
On the telephone we greet, say who we are, say why we call, listen carefully, repeat important information (time, price, place) and say goodbye.
“Hello, good morning. This is Ayuk. I would like to book a seat to Bamenda for Saturday.” “The bus leaves at 7 a.m. The ticket costs 4 500 francs.” “So, 7 a.m. and 4 500 francs. Thank you. Goodbye.”

support.title: Telephone dialogue
support.text:
AGENT: Hello, Mbengwi Express. Can I help you?
AYUK: Good morning. I would like a seat to Bamenda on Saturday, please.
AGENT: The bus leaves at 7 a.m. The ticket is 4 500 francs.
AYUK: 7 a.m., 4 500 francs. Thank you. Goodbye.

lessons.model: Two adults act the call; one writes the time and the price while listening.
lessons.guided: Act the call with a partner. Then listen to a new call and write the destination, time and price.
lessons.exercise: At what time does the bus leave?
lessons.remediation: Listen for one piece of information at a time: first the time, then the price.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, take a telephone message and write it down.
lessons.materials: Two toy phones or cups, paper.

practice.prompt: Put the telephone call in order.
items: I would like a seat to Bamenda.

practice.prompt: Why do we repeat the time and the price?
Listen and write the destination.
practice.listen: Good afternoon. The bus to Ebolowa leaves at three p.m. The ticket costs three thousand francs.

lessons.title: An adventure story: the canoe on the Sanaga
lessons.objective: Read a picture adventure story, put oneself in the place of a character and deduce the lesson.
lessons.course: An adventure story has exciting events: a problem, danger, courage and a solution. We follow the events, imagine how the characters feel and look for the lesson.

support.title: An original adventure story
support.text: Ngum and her cousin Etah crossed the Sanaga by canoe to visit their grandmother. Halfway, the wind became strong and water entered the canoe. Etah wanted to stand up, but Ngum said: “Sit down and keep calm!” The boatman gave them a bowl to remove the water. Together they reached the other bank safely. Grandmother hugged them and said: “Calm heads save lives.”

lessons.model: The adult reads the story and stops at the problem: “What would you do?”
lessons.guided: Read the story. Draw three pictures (the start, the danger, the end). Say how Ngum felt and what you would have done.
lessons.exercise: What did the boatman give the children?
lessons.remediation: Retell the story with three pictures.
lessons.transfer: Tell the story to a younger child and ask what the lesson is.

practice.prompt: Put the events in order.
items: The children got into the canoe.
They removed the water with a bowl.

practice.prompt: What is the lesson of the story?
Draw the most exciting moment of the story.
practice.answer: A drawing of the danger on the river.
practice.explanation: Show the wind and the water.

lessons.title: A narrative essay: a journey I made
lessons.objective: Write a narrative essay of about 60 words telling events in order.
lessons.course:
A narrative tells a story in the past. Plan it:
• Introduction: when, where, who (“Last holiday, I travelled to Ebolowa with my uncle.”).
• Body: events in order with first, then, after that, suddenly.
• Conclusion: how it ended and how you felt.
Use past verbs: travelled, saw, arrived, ate.
lessons.model: The adult tells a short journey aloud, raising a finger for each event, then writes the introduction.
lessons.guided: Plan your story with four boxes (when/where/who, event 1, event 2, the end). Write it in about 60 words.
lessons.exercise: Which tense do we mostly use in a narrative?
lessons.remediation: Tell the story orally first, then write one sentence per box.
lessons.transfer: Write about a journey of a family member after asking him or her about it.
lessons.materials: Paper, a plan with four boxes.

practice.prompt: Put the connecting words in a logical order.
practice.explanation: These words show the order of events.

practice.prompt: Complete with the past.
practice.text: We [[arrived]] at noon and we [[ate]] rice.

practice.prompt: Write your narrative essay: a journey I made.
practice.answer: A narrative of about 60 words with events in order.
practice.explanation: Use past verbs and connecting words.

lessons.title: Prepositions of location, direction, time and relationship
lessons.objective: Use prepositions of location, direction, time and relationship correctly in sentences.
lessons.course:
Location: in, on, under, beside, between, behind, in front of. Direction: to, from, into, out of, across, along, towards. Time: at (7 o’clock), on (Monday), in (May, the morning), before, after, during. Relationship: with, without, for, about.
“The bus left from Yaoundé at 6 a.m. and drove along the highway towards Douala with forty passengers.”
lessons.model: The adult describes a trip with gestures: “We walked across the bridge, towards the market, after breakfast.”
lessons.guided: Describe a picture of a motor park using five prepositions. Complete sentences with at, on and in.
lessons.remediation: Learn at/on/in with clock, days and months first.
lessons.transfer: Explain the way from your house to school using direction prepositions.

practice.prompt: Complete with at, on or in.
practice.explanation: on + day; at + clock time; in + month.

practice.prompt: Match each preposition with its kind.
practice.answer: across: direction; under: location; during: time.

practice.prompt: Which preposition fits: She travelled … her brother.

lessons.title: The number line: positive and negative numbers
lessons.objective: Locate positive and negative numbers on a number line and solve simple problems.
lessons.course:
Numbers below zero are negative: −1, −2, −3. They are on the left of 0 on the number line. Positive numbers are on the right.
We use negative numbers for floors under the ground (−1 = basement), temperatures below zero, or a debt.
On the line, the number on the right is always greater: −2 > −5.
lessons.model: The adult draws a number line from −10 to 40 and shows a lift going from floor 3 down to floor −1: 4 floors.
lessons.guided: Draw a number line from −10 to 40. Place ten numbers. Solve lift and temperature problems by counting jumps.
lessons.remediation: Use a thermometer picture to see numbers below zero.
lessons.transfer: Look for negative numbers in a building lift or on a weather map.
lessons.materials: Number line drawn on the floor.

practice.prompt: A bus station has a car park on floor −2. You go up 5 floors. Which floor?
On the number line, where are negative numbers?
How many jumps from −4 to 6?

lessons.title: Time: a.m., p.m. and a bus timetable
lessons.objective: Tell time using a.m. and p.m., quarter to, quarter past and half past, and use a timetable.
lessons.course:
a.m. = from midnight to midday; p.m. = from midday to midnight. 7:00 a.m. is in the morning; 7:00 p.m. is in the evening.
7:15 = quarter past seven; 7:30 = half past seven; 7:45 = quarter to eight.
Duration: a bus leaving at 8:30 a.m. and arriving at 11:00 a.m. travels for 2 hours 30 minutes.
lessons.model: The adult reads a bus timetable: “Buea 6:45 a.m., Kumba 8:15 a.m.” and calculates the journey: 1 h 30 min.
lessons.guided: Read a timetable of four buses. Write departure, arrival and duration. Set times on a clock face.
lessons.exercise: A bus leaves at 9:15 a.m. and arrives at 11:45 a.m. How long is the journey?
lessons.remediation: Count the hours first, then the minutes.
lessons.transfer: Note the times of your family’s activities with a.m. and p.m.

lessons.title: Capacity: ml, cl, dl and litres for the journey
lessons.objective: Establish the relationship between ml, cl, dl and l and convert between them.
lessons.course:
1 l = 10 dl = 100 cl = 1 000 ml. A small water bottle often holds 50 cl = 500 ml; a big one 1.5 l = 150 cl.
To convert l into ml, multiply by 1 000; ml into l, divide by 1 000.
lessons.model: The adult pours a 1 l bottle into 4 glasses of 25 cl each.
lessons.guided: Read the capacity on five bottles and containers. Convert each into ml and cl.
lessons.exercise: How many millilitres are there in 2 l?
lessons.remediation: Fill a 1 l bottle with 10 cups of 10 cl.
lessons.transfer: Calculate how much water your family needs for a trip.

practice.prompt: How many 50 cl bottles fill 3 l?

Which holds more?
practice.explanation: 1.5 l = 150 cl, more than 100 cl or 90 cl.

lessons.title: 3-D shapes: faces, edges and vertices of luggage and buildings
lessons.objective: Identify 3-D shapes and count their faces, edges and vertices.
lessons.course: Cube: 6 square faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices (a die). Cuboid: 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices (a suitcase, a box). Cylinder: 2 circular faces and 1 curved face (a tin). Cone: 1 circular face, 1 vertex. Sphere: 1 curved face (a ball). Square-based pyramid: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices.
lessons.model: The adult holds a suitcase and counts its faces, edges and vertices with the children.
lessons.guided: Collect five objects with different shapes. Count faces, edges and vertices and fill a table.
lessons.exercise: How many vertices does a cuboid have?
lessons.remediation: Mark each counted edge with a small piece of tape.
lessons.transfer: Find a cylinder, a cuboid and a sphere at home.
lessons.materials: Boxes, tins, a ball, a die.

practice.prompt: Match each object with its shape.
practice.answer: tin: cylinder; suitcase: cuboid; ball: sphere.

practice.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?
Which shape has one vertex and one circular face?
practice.explanation: A cone has a point and a circle.

lessons.title: How a road is built and maintained
lessons.objective: Describe the steps of building a good road and ways of maintaining it.
lessons.course:
Steps to build a road: survey and plan the route, clear the land, level and compact the ground, lay layers of stones and gravel, dig gutters (drains) on both sides, cover with tar (asphalt) or laterite, paint lines and put signs.
Maintenance: clean the gutters so water flows, fill potholes quickly, do not overload trucks, do not dump rubbish on the road.
lessons.model: The adult describes a road under construction: the bulldozer, the roller, the gutters.
lessons.guided: Put the steps of road construction in order. Build a small model road in sand with gutters, then pour water to test it.
lessons.remediation: Use pictures of the five main steps.
lessons.transfer: Observe a road near your home and note one problem and one solution.

practice.prompt: Put the steps in order.
practice.explanation: A road is built in layers.

practice.prompt: Which machine flattens the ground?

lessons.title: Comment aller à la gare routière ?
lessons.course:
Pour demander : « Pardon, monsieur, où est la gare routière ? » « Comment aller à l’hôpital, s’il vous plaît ? »
Pour répondre : « Allez tout droit. Prenez la deuxième rue à gauche. Traversez le pont. Continuez jusqu’au carrefour. La gare est à droite, en face de la station-service. »

support.title: Dialogue
support.text:
— Pardon, madame, comment aller à la gare routière ?
— Allez tout droit, puis prenez la première rue à droite. La gare est en face de la pharmacie.
— Merci beaucoup !

lessons.model: L’adulte trace un plan simple et décrit le chemin de l’école à la gare en suivant avec le doigt.
lessons.guided: Sur un plan, décris trois itinéraires. Ton partenaire suit avec le doigt.
lessons.answer: Comment aller à la gare, s’il vous plaît ?
accept: Comment aller à la gare, s'il vous plaît
Comment aller à la gare, s’il vous plaît
Comment aller à la gare, s’il vous plaît ?

lessons.transfer: Explique en français le chemin de ta maison au marché.

practice.answer: Tout droit, deuxième à gauche, le pont, la gare à droite.

practice.prompt: Dessine ton itinéraire de la maison à l’école et écris deux indications.

lessons.title: Finding our way: cardinal points and the compass
lessons.objective: Use orientation instruments and the sun to position things and places.
lessons.course:
The four cardinal points are North, South, East and West. The sun rises in the East and sets in the West. At midday, if you stand with your right arm to the East, you face North.
A compass has a needle that always points North. Maps usually have North at the top.
In Cameroon, Garoua is north of Yaoundé; Douala is west of Yaoundé.
lessons.model: In the morning, the adult points to the rising sun: “That is East.” Then shows North with a compass or a phone.
lessons.guided: In the school yard, find the four cardinal points with the sun. Say where the classroom, the gate and the toilets are.
lessons.remediation: Learn the order: North, East, South, West, clockwise.
lessons.transfer: Find which direction your house door faces.
lessons.materials: A compass or a phone, a map of Cameroon.

practice.prompt: Where does the needle of a compass point?
Match each town with its position from Yaoundé.
practice.explanation: Look at a map of Cameroon.

practice.prompt: Draw a compass rose with the four cardinal points.
practice.answer: A compass rose with N, E, S, W.

lessons.title: Food for the journey: salting, drying and smoking
lessons.objective: Conserve different types of food and prepare food hygienically for a journey.
lessons.course:
Food spoils because of germs, heat and humidity. We conserve it by drying (removing water: maize, fish, cassava), salting (salt draws water out: fish, meat), smoking (fish, meat over a fire) and frying.
For a journey: choose dry or well-cooked food, wrap it in clean leaves or containers, keep it in the shade, carry clean water.
lessons.model: The adult shows dried fish and smoked fish and explains why they last longer than fresh fish.
lessons.guided: Prepare a list of food for a two-day journey and explain how each one is kept safe.
lessons.exercise: Name one way to conserve fish.
lessons.answer: For example: smoking, drying or salting.
lessons.remediation: Learn two ways first: drying and smoking.
lessons.transfer: Help to prepare food for a family trip hygienically.

practice.prompt: Match each method with what it removes or adds.

practice.answer: Because of germs, heat and humidity.
practice.explanation: Germs grow in warm, wet food.

lessons.title: Dances from the regions of Cameroon
lessons.objective: Reproduce dance steps from various parts of the country and perform at least one dance step.
lessons.course:
Each region has dances: the bikutsi of the Centre (fast steps and shoulder movements), the makossa of the Littoral, the assiko of the Bassa people, the ben skin of the West, the njang of the North West, and many traditional dances in the North.
When we learn a dance, we follow the rhythm, start slowly and respect its meaning.
lessons.model: The adult shows two simple steps of a regional dance with a clapped rhythm.
lessons.guided: Learn one step from two different regions. Present them to the class and say where they come from.
lessons.exercise: Which region does the bikutsi come from?
lessons.remediation: Learn one step with clapping only.
lessons.transfer: Ask a family member to teach you a dance from your region.
lessons.materials: Drum or recorded music, open space.

practice.prompt: Match each dance with its region.

Show one dance step and say its region.
practice.answer: A step performed with its region named.

lessons.title: Throwing a disc safely
lessons.objective: Combine actions to throw a light disc and choose a good position for throwing.
lessons.course:
For the discus, we hold the disc flat with the fingers over the edge, swing the arm back, turn the body and release the disc from the index finger so it spins forward. At school we use a light plastic disc or a flying disc.
Safety: one thrower at a time, others behind, collect only on the signal.
lessons.model: The adult shows the grip, a standing throw and the release with spin.
lessons.guided: Throw a light disc five times from standing. Mark the best throw with a stick and measure with steps.
lessons.exercise: Where do the others stand during a throw?
lessons.remediation: Practise the swing without releasing the disc.
lessons.transfer: Play a disc game with friends following the safety rule.
lessons.materials: Light plastic disc or flying disc, sticks.

practice.prompt: Throws: 9 m, 12 m, 10 m. What is the best throw in metres?

practice.answer: Flat, with the fingers over the edge.

lessons.title: Describing an enthronement
lessons.objective: Use appropriate words to describe a significant life event such as the enthronement of a traditional ruler and draw lessons from it.
lessons.course: An enthronement is the ceremony where a new traditional ruler (Fon, chief, Lamido…) takes his place. It may include rites by notables, the presentation of the new ruler to the people, dances, music, gifts and a feast. It shows the continuity of the community and respect for its traditions.
lessons.model: An elder describes an enthronement he attended: the rites, the dances, the clothes.
lessons.guided: Ask an elder about an enthronement. Describe it in four sentences using some words of the family language.
lessons.answer: The ceremony where a new traditional ruler takes his place.
accept: a ceremony for a new ruler
the ceremony where a new traditional ruler takes his place
when a new chief is installed
The ceremony where a new traditional ruler takes his place
lessons.remediation: Describe one part of the ceremony: the dances or the clothes.
lessons.transfer: Share what you learnt with your class.

practice.prompt: What does an enthronement show?
practice.explanation: A new ruler continues the line.

practice.explanation: Say who, what, how people felt.

practice.prompt: Name one element of an enthronement.
practice.answer: For example: dances, gifts or the presentation of the ruler.

lessons.title: Using a web browser: addresses and links
lessons.objective: Open a web browser, key in a web address and navigate with hyperlinks to obtain useful information.
lessons.course:
A web browser is a program to visit websites: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Safari. The address bar is where we type a web address (for example www.example.org). A hyperlink is a word or picture we click to go to another page; the pointer often becomes a small hand. The Back button returns to the previous page.
We use the internet with an adult, for useful information.
lessons.model: The adult opens a browser, types an address, clicks a link and uses the Back button.
lessons.guided: With an adult, open a browser, find information for a school topic (for example Mount Cameroon) and note the website’s name.
lessons.exercise: Where do we type a web address?
lessons.remediation: Practise only the Back button and one link first.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, find the weather for your town on the internet.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.
pairs: click to go to another page
